package_info.package_manager: N/A (SaaS platform, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: All versions affected as of January 10, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: The entire backend is considered vulnerable due to a misconfiguration that allows any unauthenticated user to register and gain full read/write access to sensitive user data, including PII and plaintext passwords. This enables attackers to exfiltrate confidential information and impersonate users, violating basic security expectations for SaaS platforms.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the database security rules allow any user to read and write all data in the Firebase backend, enabling unrestricted access and modification of sensitive user information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing unauthenticated or arbitrary users to read and write all data is a critical security flaw, exposing all stored information to potential attackers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict database access to authenticated and authorized users only; the actual behavior allows global access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Open test databases during development may temporarily use permissive rules, but never in production.
key_indicators: '.read': true and '.write': true at the root level
No authentication or authorization checks in database rules

execution_context.file_location: Application backend logic (admin privilege escalation endpoint)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a super admin can activate 'ghost' mode to impersonate any user, gaining full access to their account and sensitive data, including billing information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Impersonation features without strict auditing or user notification can be abused for unauthorized access and privacy violations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict admin access to user data and require explicit consent or logging; actual behavior allows silent, full impersonation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Customer support tools may allow limited impersonation for troubleshooting, but with strict controls and transparency.
key_indicators: Access to billing and confidential data via admin features

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers a new user account via the public registration feature.
attack_chain.leads_to: Gains full read/write access to the backend database.

attack_chain.action: Attacker enumerates and exfiltrates sensitive data (names, emails, phone numbers, plaintext passwords, confidential messages, etc.) from the database.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of user privacy and potential credential theft.

attack_chain.action: If attacker escalates privileges or compromises a super admin account, they can activate 'ghost' mode to impersonate any user and access billing or other confidential information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full account takeover and access to sensitive business data.

behavioral_signatures: Unrestricted read/write operations to Firebase database from unauthenticated or newly registered users
Frequent or bulk data access patterns from non-privileged accounts
Activation of admin impersonation features without corresponding audit logs or user notifications
file_indicators: Firebase security rules with '.read': true and '.write': true at the root
Backend code enabling user impersonation or 'ghost' mode
network_indicators: Unusual API calls to Firebase endpoints from untrusted IPs
Large data transfers from endpoints associated with sensitive user data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Firebase security rules for overly permissive settings (e.g., '.read': true, '.write': true). Audit backend code for impersonation features and ensure all admin actions are logged and trigger user notifications. Analyze access logs for bulk data access or unusual activity from new or unauthenticated users. Set up alerts for large data exports or access to sensitive fields (e.g., plaintext passwords, billing info) by non-privileged accounts.
